chapter: Brother's trumpet and the early players
title: How high his brother could play and Zeb Linares
summary: His brother reached high F, confirmed by clarinetist Zeb Linares, whose death is placed around 1942.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: How high could your brother go?

How high could your brother go? Well, the fellas say he made F on the trumpet, above the staff. F. One day he made F. When they didn't drink that night, he was feeling good. He'd come out there and he made F. And E and all that stuff. He used to go so much, it almost sounded like a whistle. But the tone was clad the crystal, he'd make it clad. And I'll tell you how they know that. You see the fellas just take them on the clarinet. The fella called Zeb, you know, he was playing with us then. And he used to make that note on his clarinet, he said, man he made F.
What was Zeb's last name? Do you know?
Let me see. Zeb Linares, I think it was. Zeb Linares. He was living there on Tala Don Street.
He was on Tala Don. I think that's where he was living at. Yeah.
Do you know when he died? How long ago?

Well no, he died, let's see where he was at, the last time he came in. Because he was in the Tennessee hospital, veteran hospital, you know. And they told him not to drink so he came in and went to drink. And I can't remember them, see I can't remember them years. But I can remember these activities, you know. Was it before?
Was it before? Did he die before your brother or after?
Oh no, he died before my brother. Oh before?
Was that before World War II or after? Or during?

Oh no, I think that Zeb died there. I think he died after World War II. That's the time I think he died. You remember I say that because we were playing somewhere and my brother was playing and he came and visited us, you see. I don't know, somebody started him off with drinking.
It was before 1942 then probably. I think somewhere around there.
You were still playing when he died? Who? When Zeb died you were still playing?
Oh yeah, I just was on in 42. Yeah so. Yeah, it was the Budweiser dance hall. I'll never forget that in 42.
